source.basis: Operator location page, structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.address: Elk Grove Village, IL (EdgeConneX Chicago campus)
profile.reading: EdgeConneX CHI01 sits in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, part of EdgeConneX Chicago-area campus. Per the operator own Chicago market page, CHI01 is fully occupied and carries 24 megawatts of capacity, with a facility graphic on that page labeling it Est. 2017, though that year appears only as a graphic label rather than confirmed in the page running text, so it is presented here with that caveat rather than as fully certain. No street address, square footage, or named tenant specific to CHI01 is disclosed. The same Chicago campus later expanded with CHI02, described elsewhere on the same page as a 282,000 square foot raised-floor Phase 1 building with 7 megawatts of N plus 1 capacity, and with CHI03, at 22.4 megawatts, and most recently CHI04, announced in an August 2025 press release as a more than 30 megawatt facility being built for AI-compute customer Lambda, with 23 megawatts single-tenant and service targeted for 2026, a rare instance of EdgeConneX naming a specific anchor tenant publicly. Those additional buildings are distinct from CHI01 and should not be conflated with it. EdgeConneX is a US-based edge and build-to-suit data center operator founded in 2009 and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia, acquired by EQT Infrastructure in 2020 with Sixth Street also holding a board seat. EdgeConneX describes its footprint today as more than 90 data centers across more than 60 markets in over 20 countries on four continents, operating a joint venture called AdaniConneX in India alongside a strategic investment in the China-based operator Chayora. Elk Grove Village sits in the O Hare International Airport industrial corridor northwest of downtown Chicago, an area that has become a significant data center cluster in the Midwest given its proximity to major fiber routes, the airport itself, and the interstate highway network, a pattern reflected in EdgeConneX own decision to build multiple successive facilities, CHI01 through CHI04, on essentially the same campus over time rather than scattering them across the metro area.
profile.research_note: 24 MW and fully-occupied status confirmed via EdgeConneX own Chicago market page. Est. 2017 is a graphic-label date on that page, not confirmed in running text, flagged accordingly rather than stated as fully certain. CHI02/CHI03/CHI04 context included to distinguish this record from those separate buildings on the same campus.

reading.body:
EdgeConneX CHI01 in Elk Grove Village publishes 24 MW of critical IT power and is reported by the operator as fully occupied. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this would correspond to roughly 600 racks, though the operator has not published capacity in those terms. The facility holds ENERGY STAR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC 2 Type 2, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it to host regulated workloads and systems subject to healthcare and payment security requirements.

Within Illinois, this campus ranks seventh by published capacity among 44 mapped facilities in the state, accounting for roughly 10 percent of the 236 MW of published data center IT load currently documented here. Only six facilities in the state publish power figures at all, making CHI01 part of a small set of disclosed assets.

The site sits 6 miles from O'Hare International Airport and 25 miles from downtown Chicago. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on factors not published by the operator: the availability of grid power for expansion, the cost and timing of that power, and the actual tenant mix now occupying the reported full capacity.
